$$\begin{array}{l}
x-n y+z=6 \\
x+(n-2) y+(n+1) z=8 \\

\end{array}$$
Has a unique solution is $\frac{\mathrm{k}}{6}$, then the sum of k and all possible values of n is :

(4)

x+(n-2) y+(n+1) z \\
(n-1) y+z=1 \\

1 & -n & 1 \\
1 & (n-2) & n+1 \\
0 & n-1 & 1
\end{array}\right| \neq 0 \\
\Rightarrow n^{2}-3 n+2 \neq 0 \\
n \neq 1,2

for unique solution $\mathrm{n}=3,4,5,6$
